files.lesson.md: --- order: 15 unit: binomials node: AC9M9A02 n1 uses: [AC9M8A01 n1] assumes: [AC9M9A01 n1, AC9M9A01 n2, AC9M9A01 n3] # only x × x = x², from Year 8 index laws; the Year 9 index laws come in Irrational numbers and index laws connection: garden-extend title: Two brackets summary: "(x + 4)(x + 3) is the area of a rectangle x + 4 wide and x + 3 tall. Cut it into four pieces, x², 3x, 4x and 12, and add them: x² + 7x + 12." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "Make a garden bed longer and wider at the same time, and the new area comes in pieces. How many pieces, and how big?" app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8340 url: http://127.0.0.1:8340/index.html readySelector: "#sl-p" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: binomial.yml#explain-pic, caption: "$(x + 4)(x + 3)$: one $x^2$, $4x$ and $3x$, and 12 ones make $x^2 + 7x + 12$." } explainClip: query: { code: "@binomial.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Two brackets make four pieces" say: "Two brackets make a rectangle, and the rectangle has four pieces." clip: - caption: { text: "(x + 2)(x + 3): x + 2 across, x + 3 down.", say: "x plus two across, and x plus three down." } - wait: 600 - caption: { text: "Four pieces: x², 2x, 3x and 6. Together: x² + 5x + 6.", say: "Four pieces: x squared, two x, three x, and six." } - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "Make the 2 a −1: the strip and the corner turn negative.", say: "Make the two a minus one. That strip and the corner turn negative." } - click: Make p smaller - click: Make p smaller - click: Make p smaller - expect: { selector: "#tsum", contains: "x² + 2x − 3" } - wait: 1400 --- In Year 8 you expanded one bracket: $3(x + 2) = 3x + 6$. Now both things being multiplied are brackets, and a picture shows what happens. ## Predict: the bigger garden ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to an area for the bigger bed before building it shows who multiplies only the firsts and the lasts (x² + 12) and who sees the two strips." check: type: predict q: "The garden bed becomes $x + 4$ metres long and $x + 3$ metres wide. Which expression is its area?" options: - "$x^2 + 7x + 12$" - "$x^2 + 12$" - "$x^2 + 7x + 7$" - "$2x + 7$" actual: "x² + 7x + 12. The new bed is four pieces: the x by x square, a 4 by x strip, a 3 by x strip and the old 4 by 3 corner, which is 12. x² + 12 leaves out the two strips." ``` Your school's veggie garden is a 4 m by 3 m bed. The garden club wants it bigger: $x$ metres longer and $x$ metres wider. They haven't decided what $x$ is yet. What's the area of the whole new bed? Make a guess before you build it. ## Run: build the rectangle ```step stage: run insight: "Building (x + p)(x + q) as a rectangle and counting the pieces shows four parts: x², the two strips, and the corner." try: { playground: board, starter: "binomial.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Set the board to $(x + 4)(x + 3)$ and count the pieces. Was your prediction right?", when: "p = 4 and q = 3" } ``` $p$ is the number in the first bracket and $q$ the number in the second. The board draws the rectangle and counts what's inside. ## Investigate: four pieces ```step stage: investigate insight: "Each term in the first bracket multiplies each term in the second: four products, then collect the two x terms. Ali multiplies only the firsts and the lasts." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Expand $(x + 5)(x + 2)$. Type $x^2$ as x^2." answer: "x^2 + 7x + 10" form: expanded feedback: - ["x^2 + 10", "That's only the first pieces and the last. The two strips are 2x and 5x."] - ["x^2 + 7x + 7", "The corner is 5 × 2, not 5 + 2."] - ["2x + 7", "x times x is x², not 2x."] explain: "x × x = x², x × 2 = 2x, 5 × x = 5x, 5 × 2 = 10. Collect: x² + 7x + 10." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#ali" text: "Ali expands $(x + 3)(x + 2)$. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 4 fault: logic misconception: binomial-two-terms explain: "Line 4: Ali left out the two strips, 2x and 3x. Every term in one bracket multiplies every term in the other: x² + 2x + 3x + 6 = x² + 5x + 6." - check: type: answer q: "Expand $(x + 4)(x - 3)$." answer: "x^2 + x - 12" form: expanded feedback: - ["x^2 + x + 12", "4 × (−3) is −12."] - ["x^2 + 7x - 12", "One strip is +4x and the other is −3x: together, +x."] - ["x^2 - 12", "The strips are 4x and −3x. They don't cancel: together they're x."] explain: "x² − 3x + 4x − 12 = x² + x − 12." ``` ### Four pieces Here's the garden bed worked out, piece by piece. ```worked (x + 4)(x + 3) :: The rectangle: x + 4 across, x + 3 down. x \times x = x^2 :: The big square. x \times 3 = 3x :: One strip. 4 \times x = 4x :: The other strip. 4 \times 3 = 12 :: The corner: the old bed. x^2 + 3x + 4x + 12 = x^2 + 7x + 12 :: Collect the two strips. ``` Now try one on paper, piece by piece like the example: $(x + 5)(x + 2)$. Then type your answer. ### Find the mistake Read Ali's working. How many pieces should there be? ### A negative The second bracket takes 3 away. On the board, a negative strip is red. Which pieces turn negative? ## Modify: one change at a time ```step stage: modify insight: "One change at a time: a negative in one bracket, then both, then the same number with opposite signs (the strips cancel), then a bracket squared." try: { playground: board, starter: "binomial.yml#vary", height: 620 } tasks: - hint: "Set p to −2 and q to 5. Which strip is red?" check: { type: answer, q: "Expand $(x - 2)(x + 5)$. Build it on the board to check.", answer: "x^2 + 3x - 10", form: expanded, feedback: [["x^2 + 3x + 10", "−2 × 5 is −10."], ["x^2 - 3x - 10", "The strips are −2x and +5x: together, +3x."]], explain: "x² + 5x − 2x − 10 = x² + 3x − 10." } - hint: ["Both p and q are negative.", "The corner is −3 × −4: a negative times a negative."] check: { type: answer, q: "Expand $(x - 3)(x - 4)$.", answer: "x^2 - 7x + 12", form: expanded, feedback: [["x^2 - 7x - 12", "−3 × (−4) is +12."], ["x^2 + 7x + 12", "Both strips are negative: −3x and −4x."]], explain: "x² − 4x − 3x + 12 = x² − 7x + 12." } smaller: check: { type: "number", q: "Just the corner: what's $-3 \\times (-4)$?", answer: 12, explain: "A negative times a negative is positive: +12." } - hint: "Set p to 6 and q to −6. What happens to the two strips?" check: { type: answer, q: "Expand $(x + 6)(x - 6)$.", answer: "x^2 - 36", form: expanded, feedback: [["x^2 + 36", "6 × (−6) is −36."], ["x^2 + 12x - 36", "The strips are +6x and −6x. They cancel."]], explain: "x² − 6x + 6x − 36 = x² − 36. The strips cancel." } - hint: ["$(x + 3)^2$ means $(x + 3)(x + 3)$.", "Set p and q both to 3: two strips of 3x."] check: { type: answer, q: "Edge case: expand $(x + 3)^2$.", answer: "x^2 + 6x + 9", form: expanded, feedback: [["x^2 + 9", "That leaves out the two strips. (x + 3)² is (x + 3)(x + 3): four pieces."], ["x^2 + 3x + 9", "There are two strips of 3x: 6x."]], explain: "(x + 3)(x + 3) = x² + 3x + 3x + 9 = x² + 6x + 9." } ``` ### A negative in one bracket Each task changes one thing. Set the board, then type the expansion. ### Both negative ### Strips that cancel ### A bracket squared ## Practise: expand and collect ```step stage: practise insight: "Expanding with each sign combination, mixed; the review keeps one bracket fresh." tasks: - check: type: answer q: "Expand $(x + 7)(x + 1)$." answer: "x^2 + 8x + 7" form: expanded feedback: - ["x^2 + 7", "The two strips are x and 7x."] explain: "x² + x + 7x + 7 = x² + 8x + 7." - check: type: answer q: "Expand $(x - 5)(x + 2)$." answer: "x^2 - 3x - 10" form: expanded feedback: - ["x^2 + 3x - 10", "The strips are +2x and −5x: together, −3x."] - ["x^2 - 3x + 10", "−5 × 2 is −10."] explain: "x² + 2x − 5x − 10 = x² − 3x − 10." - check: type: answer q: "Expand $(x - 6)(x - 2)$." answer: "x^2 - 8x + 12" form: expanded feedback: - ["x^2 - 8x - 12", "−6 × (−2) is +12."] explain: "x² − 2x − 6x + 12 = x² − 8x + 12." smaller: check: { type: "answer", q: "Just the two strips: what's $-6x$ and $-2x$ together?", answer: "-8x", explain: "Both strips are negative: −6x − 2x = −8x." } - check: type: answer q: "Review: expand $3(2x - 4)$." answer: "6x - 12" form: expanded feedback: - ["6x - 4", "The 3 multiplies the 4 as well."] explain: "3 × 2x = 6x and 3 × (−4) = −12." ``` ### Both positive ### One negative ### Both negative ### Review One bracket, from Year 8. ## Make: back to the garden ```step stage: make insight: "Coming back to the opening bed: the expansion is the area for any x, and putting a number in shows how much of the new bed is new." tasks: - hint: ["The bed is (x + 4) by (x + 3).", "Four pieces: x², 3x, 4x and 12."] check: type: answer q: "Write the area of the new garden bed, $(x + 4)(x + 3)$, expanded." answer: "x^2 + 7x + 12" form: expanded feedback: - ["x^2 + 12", "That's the big square and the old bed. Add the two strips."] explain: "x² + 3x + 4x + 12 = x² + 7x + 12." - hint: ["Put x = 2 into x² + 7x + 12.", "4 + 14 + 12."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "The club picks $x = 2$. How many square metres is the new bed, and how much of that is new garden?" steps: - ["$2^2 + 7 \\times 2 + 12 = 4 + 14 + 12 = 30$ m²", "put x = 2 into the expansion"] - ["$6 \\times 5 = 30$ m²", "check: the bed is 6 m by 5 m"] - ["$30 - 12 = 18$ m² of new garden", "the old bed was 4 × 3 = 12"] answer: "18" answerLabel: "New garden (m²)" feedback: - ["30", "That's the whole bed. Take away the old 12 m²."] - ["4", "That's only the big square. The strips are new garden too."] criteria: - "I found the whole area two ways: the expansion, and 6 × 5." - "I took away the old bed." - "My new garden is more than the old bed's 12 m²." explain: "30 − 12 = 18 m² of new garden: more than the whole old bed." ``` ### The new area Back to the garden club. Sketch the bed with its four pieces on paper first. ### Pick a size **Also used in** - **Mental maths.** $47 \times 53$ is $(50 - 3)(50 + 3)$: the strips cancel, so it's $2500 - 9 = 2491$. - **Frames and borders.** A photo with a border of even width all round: the framed area is two brackets. - **Next lessons.** Spotting the pattern so you can skip the rectangle, then running it backwards to factorise. ```teacher summary: Students build (x + p)(x + q) as a rectangle on the board, see four pieces (x², two strips, a corner), expand every sign combination, and come back to a garden bed made bigger on two sides (AC9M9A02, node 1). time: 45 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 12 min · Practise and Make 10 min goals: - I can expand two brackets by finding all four pieces. - I can expand two brackets with negative numbers in them. - I can use an expansion to find an area. struggle: Finding all four pieces, then the signs. Ask students to sketch the rectangle and label each piece before they write anything. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need Year 8 expanding (one bracket) and multiplying negatives. The one idea: every term in one bracket multiplies every term in the other, so there are four pieces. The common mistake is multiplying only the firsts and the lasts ((x + 3)(x + 2) = x² + 6): it is planted after the worked example, in Ali's working. The board draws (x + p)(x + q) as a rectangle: the x² square, a strip of p x-tiles, a strip of q x-tiles and p × q ones. Negative pieces are red, as on the Year 8 tiles. running: - "Predict: take a show of hands. Students who chose x² + 12 multiplied the firsts and the lasts. Ask them to point to the two strips on the garden picture." - "Run: ask students to read the count under the board aloud." - "Investigate: draw the rectangle for (x + 4)(x + 3) live, label each piece at writing pace, then collect." - "Paper: the try-one after the worked example and the garden size in Make are worked on paper first. Books out, and look for four labelled pieces." - "Modify: before (x + 6)(x − 6), ask what will happen to the two strips." - "Make: ask who thinks the new garden is bigger than the old bed before anyone calculates." stuck: - see: A student writes x² + 6 for (x + 3)(x + 2) (Ali's mistake). ask: Sketch the rectangle. How many pieces are there? fix: "Four: x², 2x, 3x and 6. Every term multiplies every term." - see: A student gets the corner's sign wrong with two negatives. ask: What's a negative times a negative? fix: "Positive: (x − 3)(x − 4) has +12 in the corner." - see: A student writes 2x for x times x. ask: What's 5 times 5? So what's x times x? fix: x², the big square, not 2x. stretch: Expand (x + a)(x + b) with letters. What do the middle term and the last term have to do with a and b? support: "A blank 2 by 2 grid to fill in: the bracket terms along the top and down the side, the four products inside." leads: > This starts AC9M9A02. Where it leads: the pattern (x + a)(x + b) = x² + (a + b)x + ab (next lesson), factorising quadratics, and solving quadratics (Years 9 and 10). exit: q: Expand (x − 4)(x + 6). a: x² + 2x − 24. explain: > Two brackets multiply like the sides of a rectangle. $(x + 4)(x + 3)$ is $x + 4$ across and $x + 3$ down, so the area has four pieces: $x \times x = x^2$, $x \times 3 = 3x$, $4 \times x = 4x$ and $4 \times 3 = 12$. Add them and collect the two strips: $x^2 + 7x + 12$. Signs come with the numbers: $(x + 4)(x - 3) = x^2 - 3x + 4x - 12 = x^2 + x - 12$. ```

# region: ali
Expand (x + 3)(x + 2).
x times x is x².
3 times 2 is 6.
So (x + 3)(x + 2) = x² + 6.
